Glossary

Every term from both halves of the pack, business analysis and the method, in one A–Z. Search, or tap any underlined word anywhere in the pack. Type #notinnotes for the terms that were never in your notes.

Acceptance criteriadocument

The list of conditions that decide whether something is finished. Written before it gets built, not after — otherwise you are marking your own homework.

In the proper languageA prioritised list of criteria the finished must meet before the user will accept it, held for the project as a whole in the .

Agileprocess

Building in small pieces, showing each piece to people quickly, and expecting to change your mind as you learn. Suits situations where nobody yet knows exactly what's needed.

In the proper languageIterative and incremental delivery approach prioritising working software, customer collaboration and responsiveness to change over comprehensive up-front . An umbrella term rather than a single method.

AIO Testsnot in your notessoftware

A test-management add-on for . Holds the , records which passed and which failed, and links results back to the they test.

In the proper languageTest management application for providing test case authoring, execution cycles, and between , tests and .

Aligning products to business objectivesconcept

The improvements have to add up to something the organisation already said it wanted, including how it treats people and the planet.

In the proper language“Ultimately, the outcomes and benefits to be achieved from the project need to align with and contribute to the business objectives. These may include environmental, social and governance () goals set by the organization. The sustainability performance targets and tolerances for the project, documented in the business case, should reference and contribute to the ESG goals of the organization.”

Analysisdefinition

Breaking something complicated into parts you can look at one at a time, then working out what those parts mean together. The opposite of taking a situation at face value.

In the proper languageSystematic decomposition of a problem, process or dataset into constituent elements to establish structure, causation and relationships, producing findings that support a decision.

APIdefinition

The way two pieces of software talk to each other. Application Programming Interface. Think of it as a hatch in the side of a system with a fixed set of things you're allowed to ask for — you don't get to reach inside and rummage, you ask through the hatch in the agreed format.

In the proper languageApplication Programming Interface. A defined contract exposing a set of operations, request and response formats, and authentication , enabling systems to exchange data without knowledge of internal implementation.

Artefactdefinition

Just a formal word for a thing you produce — a document, a diagram, a spreadsheet. When someone says “ artefacts” they mean “the documents the analyst made”.

In the proper languageAny tangible work created during a project lifecycle. Used generically to encompass documents, models, registers and .

Daniel's “operational analysis artefacts” just means the documents produced when analysing day-to-day operations.

As-isdefinition

How the process really works today. Not how the official document says it works — those two are almost never the same, and the difference is usually the most interesting thing you'll find.

In the proper languageCurrent-state documenting the process as actually performed, including workarounds and exceptions, forming the for .

Assumption

Something everyone is treating as true without having actually checked. Usually the most dangerous line on the log.

In the proper languageA statement accepted as true without verification, on which planning depends; note that has no assumption register, so these surface through the risk register or the daily log.

Azuresoftware

Microsoft's platform — rented computing power and services. Often mentioned alongside , which is a separate work-tracking product with a confusingly similar name.

In the proper languageMicrosoft public cloud platform providing infrastructure, platform and application services. Distinct from , its ALM and toolchain.

Azure DevOpsnot in your notessoftware

A Microsoft for tracking work and automating builds and releases — a competitor to . Confusingly named: it is a specific tool, not the same thing as the way of working.

In the proper languageMicrosoft ALM suite comprising Boards, Repos, Pipelines, Test Plans and . A product implementing practices, not the practice itself.

Your note said “”. Daniel’s tools line says Azure DevOps, which is the product. Worth keeping the two apart.

Backlog refinementnot in your notesprocess

The ongoing job of breaking big items down, adding detail and re-ordering, so that the next things to be picked up are ready to go.

In the proper languageContinuous activity of decomposing, estimating, clarifying and reordering items to ensure upcoming work meets the .

Baseline (project baseline)definition

The agreed version of everything, frozen. It can still change, but only by asking and being told yes.

In the proper language

“The current approved versions of the and that are subject to change control.”

A is “a modification to any of the approved products that constitute the project baseline”. Everything the issues practice does hangs off those two sentences.

BAUnot in your notesdefinition

Business as usual. The ordinary day-to-day running of things, as opposed to a project that changes them.

In the proper languageBusiness as usual. Ongoing operational activity distinct from change initiatives, typically funded and governed separately.

BCSqualification

The British professional body for IT, which runs the main UK qualifications. Foundation level first, then Practitioner.

In the proper languageBCS, The Chartered Institute for IT. Awarding body for the Foundation and Practitioner Certificates in and the diploma pathway.

Benefitdefinition

The measurable improvement that follows the change — not “we launched it” but a number that moved.

In the proper language“The measurable improvement resulting from an outcome that is perceived as an advantage by the investing organization and contributes towards one or more business objectives.”

Benefits management approachapproach

The plan for going back later to check whether the promised improvements actually turned up.

In the proper language“To define the benefits management actions and benefits reviews that will be established to ensure that the project’s outcomes are achieved and to confirm that the project’s benefits are realized.” Benefit reviews “should include assessing whether sustainability targets have been achieved”. Held in the ; much of it runs after the project closes.

Benefits realisationprocess

Going back after the change is live to check whether the promised in the actually happened. Almost nobody does it, which is why so many projects can claim success.

In the proper languageConfirms after closure that forecast benefits have materialised, with defined measures, owners and review points, and is carried out by the business rather than by the team that built the thing.

Benefits tolerancedefinition

How far short the promised improvement may fall before you have to go and tell someone.

In the proper language“The permissible deviation in the benefit performance targets that is allowed before the deviation needs to be escalated to the next level of management. Benefits tolerance is documented in the business case.”

Bill of materialsnot in your notesdocument

The full parts list for something being made — every component, how many of each, and how they nest together. Usually shortened to BOM, said as “bom”.

In the proper languageHierarchical structure listing all components, sub-assemblies and quantities required to manufacture a . Maintained in and consumed by for planning and procurement.

Bluestar PLMsoftware

A product-management system that plugs straight into Microsoft and links it to engineering drawing software. It's the piece that sits between the tool and the , so a change to a drawing flows through to the parts list the factory works from.

In the proper language platform natively embedded in , supporting multi-CAD environments and synchronising structures, BOMs and engineering changes between design tools and .

Your note reads “Bluster” and runs off the edge of the photo. Given , and are on the same line, this is almost certainly Bluestar — worth checking the CV.

BPMN 2.0definition

A standard set of shapes for drawing business processes, so that everyone reads the same diagram the same way. Stands for Business and Notation.

In the proper languageOMG-maintained modelling standard defining a common notation for business process diagrams. Version 2.0 added formal execution semantics alongside the visual notation.

BRDdocument

A document saying what the business needs and why, in ordinary business language, with nothing about how it'll be built. “Customers must be able to see where their order is.”

In the proper languageBusiness Requirements Document. Captures business objectives, and high-level in solution-agnostic language, forming the basis for .

Business analysisdefinition

Working out what a business actually needs, then describing it clearly enough that someone else can build it. You sit between the people who have a problem and the people who can fix it, and your job is to make sure nothing gets lost in between.

In the proper languageThe discipline of identifying business needs and recommending that deliver value. Spans , , and of across a change initiative.

Daniel's note said “actually get a grip of what it is” — this is it.

Business analystrole

The person who works out what a business needs and describes it clearly enough that somebody else can build it. Usually shortened to BA.

In the proper languageRole accountable for eliciting, documenting and validating requirements, and for maintaining traceability between business need and delivered solution.

Business casedocument

The written argument that the job is worth doing: what it costs, what it gains, and what could spoil it.

In the proper language“To document the business justification for undertaking a project, based on the estimated costs against the expected benefits to be gained and offset by any associated risks.”

Business case (the practice)practice

The part of the work that keeps asking whether this is still worth doing, and does not stop asking once it has started.

In the proper language

“To establish mechanisms to judge whether the project is (and remains) desirable, viable, and achievable as a means to support decision-making in its continued investment.”

Desirable, viable and achievable — three adjectives, in that order.

Business case management (the technique)technique

Four steps: write it, check it, update it, look back.

In the proper language

  • Develop
  • Check
  • Maintain
  • Confirm

Memory hook

D
Develop
C
Check
M
Maintain
C
Confirm

The four in order, and the letters spell nothing — DCMC.

DangerA great deal of the material in circulation gives step 2 as verify. It is check. Verify is wording from an earlier version of the method and it survives all through older notes.

Business interestconcept

The side paying for it, and the side that has to keep getting its money’s worth.

In the proper language“Projects are created to meet a business need, which needs to be continuously justified as value for money throughout the lifetime of the project.” Represented by the .

Business layerrole

The people above all of it. They set what it is for and how much room it gets, and they are not on the team.

In the proper languageIt is “the layer of outside the project team that sets the overall objectives and levels for the project and holds the accountable for meeting them”.

Business objectivedefinition

What the organisation is trying to get better at overall. The benefits are meant to add up to these.

In the proper language“The measurable outcomes that demonstrate progress in relation to the organization’s strategy and to which the project should contribute.”

Business process improvementprocess

Making an existing process work better — faster, cheaper, fewer mistakes. Again this names an activity rather than a specific method; the methods are things like Lean and .

In the proper languageSystematic effort to improve process efficiency, quality or cost. Delivered through specific methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma or BPM rather than as a technique in itself.

Business requirementsdefinition

What the organisation needs, stated in business language with nothing about how it will be achieved. “Customers must be able to track their order” is one. “Build an order tracking page” is not — that has already jumped to a .

In the proper languageHigh-level statements of organisational need expressed in solution-agnostic terms, capturing what must be achieved and why. Sit above in the hierarchy and are captured in the .

Business validationprocess

Checking the result actually achieves what the business wanted, beyond just matching the words in the specification. You can satisfy every line of a and still miss the point.

In the proper languageConfirmation that the delivered satisfies the underlying business need and intended , as distinct from conformance to written .

CADnot in your notessoftware

Computer-Aided Design. Software for drawing physical objects precisely, usually in 3D, so they can be manufactured from the drawing. Solid Edge is one example.

In the proper languageComputer-Aided Design. Software for geometric modelling of parts and assemblies, producing the design data consumed by and manufacturing systems.

CCUUTtechnique

The memory hook for the five characteristics of a project: Change, Cross-functional, Unique, Uncertainty, Temporary.

In the proper languageA mnemonic, not a term of the method. The first letters of the five characteristics that distinguish a project from business as usual.

Ceremoniesprocess

The fixed set of meetings in : planning at the start, a short daily catch-up, a review to show what got built, and a retrospective to discuss how the team is working.

In the proper languageThe prescribed events — planning, daily scrum, sprint review and sprint retrospective — each time-boxed with a defined purpose.

Changecharacteristic

A project exists to make something different afterwards.

In the proper language“Projects are the means by which we introduce change.”

Change (to a baseline)definition

An alteration to something already agreed and frozen. Different from change as in "the thing a project exists to introduce".

In the proper languageA modification to any of the approved products that constitute the project baseline.

Change approvalprocess

The formal yes before something is allowed to go live. Someone with authority reviews what is being released, what could go wrong, and how you would undo it if it does. Even finished, fully tested work waits for this.

In the proper languageThe gate at which a release is authorised after review of risk, impact, test evidence and rollback plan; a change advisory board is the ITIL route, whereas in a stage-gated project the project board holds the authority.

Change budgetdocument

Money set aside up front for changes nobody has asked for yet, so that agreeing one does not mean reopening the whole plan.

In the proper languageA sum earmarked to fund approved changes — or a set of authorized constraints within which trade-offs can be made.

Change controlprocess

The formal route by which a change to agreed scope gets properly considered instead of just happening. Someone raises it, someone works out what it would affect, someone decides, and it gets written down.

In the proper languageThe process protecting the : requests for change and are raised, assessed for impact, decided by the or its delegate, and recorded.

Change managementconcept

Getting people to actually take up the new thing. It has nothing to do with editing documents.

In the proper language

“All projects result in a change from how people, organizations, and systems operate the current state to a future target state that incorporates the use of the project products. Effective is required to deliver this change.”

The trapChange management moves the organization to a target state; change control governs modifications to baselined products. There, “change” means “a modification to any of the approved products that constitute the ”.

Change management approachdocument

The written plan for moving people onto the new way of working.

In the proper language

“To establish the target organizational state required for the project to meet its objectives together with the means by which the business will shift from the current state and through any interim states.”

How much detail it needs depends on: the skills and capabilities required during and after the transition; which areas of the are likely to be impacted; the key relationships; the evolving ; and how best to transition.

Change requestnot in your notesdocument

A written proposal to change something that had already been agreed. Writing it down is the point: it forces someone with authority to say yes or no, rather than the change just happening.

In the proper languageKnown in as a request for change and treated as one of the five kinds of issue, which is counter-intuitive until you see that an issue is anything that has happened and needs a decision.

Check (business case step 2)technique

Keep testing the argument as the facts change, right through to the last stage.

In the proper language

“The business case may undergo further refinement and will be updated across stages as project costs, timescale, products, and risks are further understood.”

The checks it “when assessing progress, risks, and issues to determine their impact on the business justification” and “during the final stage, as part of ‘’, to assess the project’s performance against requirements and the probability that the outcomes will provide the expected benefits”.

The trapCheck covers closure, and the project manager does it; confirm happens after the project no longer exists.

Checkpoint reportdocument

How one patch of the building work is going, sent up by whoever is running that patch, at whatever interval was agreed.

In the proper languageWork package status, from the team manager to the project manager. Time-driven — the frequency is set in the work package description.

CI/CDnot in your notesprocess

The automated pipeline underneath . Every time someone changes the code it's automatically combined with everyone else's, tested, and pushed towards release.

In the proper languageContinuous and Continuous Delivery/Deployment. Automated pipeline performing build, test and release on every change, providing rapid feedback and repeatable deployment.

Closing a projectprocess

The last step, and a deliberate one rather than a project just going quiet. The thing gets formally accepted, checked against what was promised, and handed to the people who will run it from now on.

In the proper languageProvides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project is confirmed and the objectives set out in the are recognised as achieved.

Closing capability gapsconcept

You find what is missing and teach the people you have, because swapping them out is usually not on offer.

In the proper language

“It is important to understand the competencies and capabilities of the people recruited or assigned to a project and ensure any gaps are identified and mitigations established to cover them, such as upskilling.”

And realistically: “ideally organizations would select the people needed to fulfil each of the required roles, but this is often not possible.”

Cloudnot in your notesdefinition

Running software on someone else's computers, rented by the hour, instead of on machines your company owns and keeps in a cupboard.

In the proper languageDelivery of computing resources as an on-demand metered service, spanning infrastructure, platform and software service models.

Co-creationtechnique

Designing the thing together with the people who will use it, so that they actually take to it.

In the proper language

“A specific form of involving users and in the design of products and agreed ways of working to ensure they are adopted by the project and organizational ecosystems.”

The trapIt is the narrower of the two, not a synonym: who (users and key influencers), what (products and agreed ways of working), why (adoption).

Collaborationconcept

Everyone involved pulling in the same direction, rather than each guarding their own patch.

In the proper language“People from across the working together to achieve the project’s objectives.”

Commercial management approachapproach

How outside firms and money are handled: who is paid for what, on what terms.

In the proper languageHow commercial and supplier relationships are managed — contracts, procurement, and moving capability on and off the project. Held in the .

Commissioning (management level)concept

The people outside the job who set the limits, and who hold the deciders to account.

In the proper languageThe — outside the project team. “Defining the project level tolerances”; setting the overall requirements; holding the accountable.

Communication management approachdocument

The written plan for who hears what, how often, and how they answer back.

In the proper language

“To define and describe the means and frequency of communication with and receiving feedback from across the , supporting alignment and shaping of the project. It facilitates engagement with stakeholders through the establishment of a controlled and bidirectional flow of information.”

Three phrases carry it: means and frequency, receiving feedback, controlled and bidirectional. Communication here is explicitly two-way.

Concerndefinition

Something somebody has raised that needs looking at, but nobody yet knows how urgent it is or how much it matters.

In the proper languageAn issue whose timeliness and impact need to be assessed.

Confirm (business case step 4)technique

Go back once it is all over and see whether the improvement really happened.

In the proper language“The business will review the business case as part of a post-project to determine the project outcomes in realizing their benefits. They will also assess whether the intended benefits have been realized in practice.” Done by the business, after the project has closed.

Confluencenot in your notessoftware

Atlassian's documentation tool, the twin of . Jira holds the work; Confluence holds the writing about the work — , meeting notes, decisions. Almost always found together.

In the proper languageAtlassian collaborative documentation platform with page hierarchies, templates and version history. Integrates with for requirement-to-issue linking.

Continuous improvementnot in your notesprocess

Making small, ongoing improvements to how work is done rather than waiting for one big project. The idea underneath and .

In the proper languageOngoing incremental optimisation of processes and practices, institutionalised through retrospectives, kaizen activity or a formal improvement cycle such as PDCA.

Controlling a stageprocess

The day job, and it repeats for every chunk of work. Work goes out, progress comes back, problems get handled, and somebody decides what needs escalating and what does not.

In the proper languageThe assigns and monitors work, handles issues, reports progress and takes corrective action to keep the within its .

Costaspect

What the work is allowed to spend. One of the seven things a project is judged on, and one of the seven you can be given room to move on.

In the proper languageAn aspect of project performance. Tolerances are set against it at project, stage and team level, and actual progress is measured against its performance target.

Could have

Nice if there's room. First thing dropped when time runs short.

In the proper languageDesirable included only if capacity permits; the primary contingency buffer.

Cross-functionalcharacteristic

It cuts across the usual departments, and sometimes across separate companies.

In the proper language“Projects often work across the usual functional divisions within an organization and sometimes span different organizations.” A project “involves a team of people with different skills working together on a temporary basis to introduce a change that will impact others outside the team”.

CRUDnot in your notesdefinition

The four things you can do to any record: Create, Read, Update, Delete. Comes up constantly when what a user is allowed to do.

In the proper languageCreate, Read, Update, Delete. The four basic persistence operations, commonly used as a shorthand for specifying permissions per role and entity.

Cultureconcept

What a group actually values and how it behaves, as opposed to what its documents say it does.

In the proper language

Culture is “the set of shared attitudes, values, goals” of a group. It shapes how people collaborate, how openly problems get raised, and how readily change is accepted.

A project inherits the culture of the organizations involved and, through the organizing practice, deliberately develops “the project behaviours and culture” of its own .

Customer journey mappingnot in your notestechnique

Drawing the whole experience from the customer's side — every step, every point of contact, and how they feel at each one. Different from a , which shows what the organisation does; this shows what the customer goes through.

In the proper languageTechnique visualising customer experience across touchpoints and channels, capturing actions, emotions and pain points to identify improvement opportunities.

D365software

Microsoft Dynamics 365. A family of business applications covering finance, operations, sales and customer service.

In the proper languageMicrosoft Dynamics 365. Modular suite spanning and CRM functions on a shared data platform.

Daily logdocument

The scribble pad — whatever is worth noting but not worth a form.

In the proper languageThe ’s informal record: actions, events, observations and minor issues not being managed formally.

Data analysisnot in your notestechnique

Looking at the actual numbers rather than what people say happens. How many orders really fail, how long the process really takes. Evidence that settles arguments.

In the proper languageExamination of operational data to establish baselines, quantify problems and validate assumptions, typically using , spreadsheets or BI tooling.

Data modelnot in your notesdocument

A map of what information the system holds and how the different pieces relate to each other — a customer has many orders, each order has many items.

In the proper languageAbstract representation of data entities, attributes and relationships. Expressed as conceptual, logical or physical models depending on level of detail.

Databasenot in your notesdefinition

An organised store of information that software reads from and writes to. Usually arranged as tables with rows and columns, like a very strict spreadsheet.

In the proper languageStructured repository of persisted data. Relational databases organise data into normalised tables with defined keys and relationships.

Decision logdocument

A record of what was decided, by whom, when, and crucially why. Six months later the why is the only part anybody needs and the only part nobody wrote down.

In the proper languageRegister of material decisions capturing rationale, decision-maker, date and options rejected. Supports auditability and prevents re-litigation of settled questions.

Defectdefinition

Something that doesn't work as it should. Called a defect or a bug depending on how formal the organisation is.

In the proper languageA deviation between actual and specified behaviour, recorded with , , reproduction steps and environment.

Define roles, responsibilities and relationshipsprinciple

Everybody knows what they answer for and who they answer to, agreed in advance rather than worked out while it goes wrong.

In the proper language

“A PRINCE2 Project Management project has defined and agreed roles and responsibilities within an organization structure that engages the business, user, and supplier stakeholder interests.”

The reason a project needs a structure of its own: “the day-to-day line management structures of the business may not be designed for, or suited to, project work.”

DangerThe name ends with relationships. Material in circulation drops the word and calls this “defined roles and responsibilities” — that is not the full name, and relationships recur throughout the element.

Definition of Donenot in your notesdocument

A checklist a piece of work has to pass before anyone is allowed to call it finished. Different from : acceptance criteria are specific to one , the definition of done applies to every story.

In the proper languageAgreed exit criteria applying to all items — typically coded, peer-reviewed, unit tested, , documented and deployed to a test environment.

Definition of Readynot in your notesdocument

A checklist a piece of work has to pass before a team will agree to start it. Stops half-formed requests being pulled into a .

In the proper languageAgreed entry criteria a item must meet before commitment — typically estimated, with , dependencies identified and no known blockers.

Delivered against worth itconcept

Delivered on time and still not worth it is a real outcome, and a common one.

In the proper language

“For benefits to be realized, the outcomes must be achieved, which means that the outputs from the project are used as intended, new capability is defined, and barriers to the use of the new capability are identified.”

“A problem that commonly occurs is that projects are often successful from a delivery perspective but fail from an investment perspective.”

The trapTwo different tests: delivery asks whether the outputs were produced, investment asks whether the benefits were realized.

Delivering (management level)concept

The people building one patch of it, inside the room agreed for that patch.

In the proper languageThe . “Control for a , but only within the work package tolerances agreed with the project manager.”

Delivery approachapproach

The shape of the building work. The method does not care which you pick.

In the proper language

PRINCE2 does not assume or require any particular delivery approach. Three are named:

The trap“Event-driven” is not a delivery approach — it is a type of control, and it belongs to the progress practice.

Delivery teamrole

The people who actually build the thing — developers, testers, sometimes operations staff.

In the proper languageThe cross-functional group responsible for implementing, testing and deploying the .

Dependency

Something you cannot get on with until somebody else finishes their bit.

In the proper languageA relationship where progress on one item depends on another being completed, defined between products rather than activities, and either internal or external to the project.

Design the project ecosystem (organizing step 2)technique

Work out the shape of the team, and how it will behave.

In the proper language“Project organizational design describes how to organize work and people to achieve the project’s objectives. This includes: determining the effective structure of the team; determining the people and resources needed; implementing integrated working practices; developing the project behaviours and .”

Develop (business case step 1)technique

Turn the request into a first written argument for doing the work at all.

In the proper language“The provision of a activates the process of . The project mandate is then used as an input to develop the initial business justification for the project documented in the outline business case.”

Develop the project ecosystem (organizing step 3)technique

Put the design into practice, and keep changing it as the work goes on.

In the proper language“Implementing the project organizational design and adapting and evolving it as the project progresses… ensuring the project is set up to deliver its objectives and to continuously improve. The development activities may include: onboarding people to the project, for example, a site visit, induction, or certification.”

DevOpsprocess

A way of organising so that the people who build software and the people who run it are one team rather than two who blame each other. In practice it mostly means heavy automation — code gets built, tested and released by machines rather than by a person doing it by hand at midnight.

In the proper languagePractice development and operations through shared ownership, automation and continuous integration and delivery pipelines, reducing lead time and deployment risk.

Digital and data management approachapproach

How information gets created, used and looked after, both during the work and afterwards.

In the proper language“How data and information will be created, used and managed across the project ecosystem and afterwards.” Held in the PID.

Digital transformationdefinition

A very broad phrase for an organisation changing how it works by using technology differently. It describes a programme of activity rather than any particular technique, so there is not much underneath it to learn.

In the proper languageUmbrella term for organisation-wide change programmes reorienting operating models around digital capability. Non-specific by nature; treat as context rather than method.

From Ray's CV. A container word rather than a concept.

Directing (management level)concept

The people who decide whether it carries on, inside limits set above them.

In the proper languageThe . Overall direction within the constraints set by the ; “determining whether to authorize any deviation that breaches or is forecast to breach the agreed stage tolerances”.

Directing a projectprocess

The people above you decide whether the work starts, carries on, or stops, and they do it at a few fixed points along the way. You have no control over this one. What you need from it is knowing who to take a question to.

In the proper languageEnables the to be accountable for the project's success by making the key decisions, while delegating day-to-day management to the .

Dis-benefitdefinition

A measurable downside you already know is coming, and have decided the rest is worth it anyway.

In the proper languageA measurable negative consequence of an outcome: “outcomes that are perceived as negative by one or more stakeholders may result in dis-benefits”.

The trapDis-benefits are expected consequences of an activity, whereas a risk is uncertain and may never materialize.

Discovery sessionstechnique

An early meeting held to work out what the problem actually is, before anyone starts deciding what to build. Deliberately open-ended.

In the proper languageFacilitated early-phase workshop exploring the problem space, constraints and landscape prior to design.

Document analysistechnique

Reading whatever already exists — process documents, manuals, old — and then assuming most of it is out of date.

In the proper languageReview of existing documentation to establish understanding. Findings should be against observed practice, as documented process commonly diverges from actual.

Elicitationprocess

Drawing information out of people. The word matters: you are pulling it out, not collecting it. If you simply ask people what they want, you get their preferred rather than the underlying problem.

In the proper languageThe activity of drawing out from and other sources using structured techniques including , , , , and .

James's CV had “elicit (draw out) req” — that note was exactly right.

End project reportdocument

The closing write-up: how the project actually performed against what it originally said it would do. It is also where anything unfinished gets recorded, so it does not simply vanish.

In the proper languageReviews how the project performed against the version of the used to authorise it.

End stage reportdocument

The write-up of the chunk just finished: what got made, what it cost, what went wrong, and what was learned. Its job is to give the people deciding enough to say carry on, or stop.

In the proper languageProvides the with sufficient information to decide what to do next with the project.

End-to-end integrationtechnique

Following one whole transaction all the way through every system it touches, rather than testing each system on its own. Individual parts often pass while the joins between them fail.

In the proper languageTesting a complete business transaction across all components and interfaces, data flow and handoffs rather than isolated component behaviour.

Ensure continued business justificationprinciple

There has to be a good reason to start, and it has to still be a good reason later. When it stops being one, the work stops.

In the proper language

“A PRINCE2 Project Management project has business justification sufficient to warrant investment to initiate the project and ongoing investment through to successful completion. If it does not, it should be stopped.”

There “must be a justifiable reason for starting a project, and the justification must remain valid and be revalidated throughout the lifecycle of the project”. The justification “drives decision-making to ensure that the project remains aligned with the sought and contributes to ”.

Enterprise architecture standardsdefinition

The organisation-wide rules about what technology is allowed and how systems should fit together. Stops every project inventing its own approach and leaving a mess behind.

In the proper languageOrganisation-level design principles, reference models and technology standards governing how systems are structured and . is the most widely used framework.

Epicdocument

A chunk of work too big to do in one go, which gets broken down into several smaller .

In the proper languageA large body of work spanning multiple , decomposed into . Sits above story level in the hierarchy.

ERDnot in your notesdocument

The diagram of a . Entity Relationship Diagram. Boxes for the kinds of thing stored, lines for how they connect.

In the proper languageEntity Relationship Diagram. Notation depicting entities, attributes and cardinality of relationships within a .

ERPdefinition

One large system that runs most of a company's core operations — finance, stock, purchasing, HR — in one place instead of separate systems that don't talk. Enterprise Resource Planning. and are examples.

In the proper languageEnterprise Resource Planning. suite covering core business functions on a shared , typically requiring significant configuration and process alignment during implementation.

ESGdefinition

Environmental, social and governance. The three headings an organisation gets judged under for whether it behaves responsibly, beyond whether it makes money.

In the proper languageEnvironmental, social and governance. Sustainability targets in the business case reference the organization’s ESG goals.

Establishing business justificationconcept

Counting what it costs to build is not enough. What it costs to run afterwards counts too.

In the proper language“The business case should include not only the costs of developing the project product but also any changes to operational costs when the project concludes.”

Event-driven controldefinition

A check that happens because something specific has happened, rather than because a date has come round. Not a way of building anything.

In the proper language“A management control that occurs when a specific event occurs” — the end of a stage, the completion of the PID, the creation of an exception report, or an organizational event such as the end of the financial year. It belongs to the progress practice, and it is not a delivery approach.

Events

The circles. The start, the end, and anything that interrupts partway through.

In the proper language element representing something that happens during a process — start, intermediate or end — optionally typed by trigger such as message or timer.

Excelsoftware

Microsoft's spreadsheet. Still, quietly, where an enormous amount of real actually happens.

In the proper languageMicrosoft spreadsheet application. Remains the default tool for ad-hoc , data reconciliation and lightweight modelling.

Exceptiondefinition

The moment you can see you are going to end up further off course than you were allowed. You raise it when you can see it coming, not once it has already happened.

In the proper languageA forecast deviation beyond agreed — a forecast breach rather than an actual one — which triggers an exception report to the next .

Exception plandocument

A replacement plan, written when the current one is going to run out of room. Same level of detail as the one it replaces.

In the proper languageA plan produced to replace one forecast to breach its tolerance, at the same level of detail.

Exception reportdocument

The alarm. Raised when you can see you are going to overshoot what you were allowed, not once you already have.

In the proper languageRaised when a tolerance is breached or forecast to be breached, from the project manager to the project board. Event-driven.

Exception-manageddefinition

People are given room to move and left alone inside it. They go back up only when that room is about to run out.

In the proper languageOne of the four structural features of PRINCE2, following from the manage by exception principle: limits of delegated authority are established by defining tolerances for performance against the plans.

Factors that influence tailoringconcept

How much method you use is decided by what the job itself is like.

In the proper language

From the principle statement
Project environment · size · complexity · importance · delivery method · team capability · level of risk.
From the purpose of tailoring
Scale · complexity · importance · delivery method · team capability · risk.
Also
“How the method is applied and tailored depends on the nature of the project and factors internal and external to the business” — regulation, standards, corporate policy.

Features and benefits of PRINCE2concept

It fits any kind of work, it gives everyone the same words, and it keeps the managing separate from the making.

In the proper language

Generic and flexible
Its “strength is its flexibility and the fact that it is not specific to a particular industry, type of project, commercial model, project lifecycle, delivery method, product development, or engineering practice”.
A common vocabulary
It “provides a common vocabulary for all participants, which encourages consistency and the ability to reuse project assets, facilitate staff mobility, and reduce the impact of personnel changes or handovers”.
Management separated from specialist work
It tells you how to manage a project, not how to build the thing.
Four structural features
, , and — following from the principles.

The trapA common vocabulary is not a fixed one: “in general, it may be necessary to tailor the PRINCE2 Project Management terminology to what is common in the company or in the industry in which the project is taking place”.

Figmasoftware

A design tool used to draw what a screen will look like before anyone builds it. Several people can work in the same file at once.

In the proper languageCollaborative interface design platform used for wireframing, high-fidelity mock-ups and interactive , with shared component libraries.

FINOPSsoftware

Two completely different things share this name. Next to , as in your notes, it means Finance and Operations — the finance module of Microsoft's . Separately, FinOps is a discipline about controlling spending. Same word, unrelated meanings.

In the proper languageIn the Dynamics context, Finance & Operations — the enterprise module. Distinct from FinOps, the cloud financial management practice.

From Yusuf's CV, where it sits directly after , so it is the module.

Fishbone diagramnot in your notestechnique

A diagram for brainstorming everything that might have caused a problem, grouped into categories, drawn so it looks like a fish skeleton. Also called an Ishikawa diagram.

In the proper languageIshikawa cause-and-effect diagram organising candidate causes by category — commonly people, process, equipment, materials, environment, measurement — against a stated effect.

Five Whysnot in your notestechnique

Ask why something happened, then ask why again about that answer, five times over. Simple, and it usually gets you past the first plausible-sounding explanation to the real one.

In the proper languageIterative interrogative technique for , repeatedly asking why to traverse a causal chain from symptom to root cause.

Focus on productsprinciple

Agree what is being produced and what “good enough” means for each of them before deciding what anyone will do.

In the proper language

“A PRINCE2 Project Management project focuses on the definition and delivery of products, in particular their user’s quality expectations and requirements.”

The “describes the total output from the project as defined in the ”.

Forecastdefinition

A prediction of where things will end up, worked out from what has happened so far rather than from hope.

In the proper languageA prediction made by studying historical data and past patterns.

FRDdocument

A document saying what the system must actually do. This is where “customers can see their order” becomes “the order screen displays current status, refreshed every fifteen minutes.”

In the proper languageFunctional Requirements Document. Specifies system behaviour required to satisfy the , decomposed into individually testable statements.

Functional requirementdefinition

Something the system has to do. “The user can reset their password by email.”

In the proper languageA a behaviour or function the must perform, expressed so as to be individually verifiable.

Functional specificationdocument

Usually the same thing as an . Different organisations prefer different names for the same document, which is worth knowing before you assume there are two.

In the proper language of required system behaviour. In most organisations synonymous with the ; in some, a more detailed successor to it.

Future statedefinition

Another way of saying — how things will look after the change.

In the proper languageSynonym for target-state. The intended condition of processes, systems or capabilities following the change.

Gap analysistechnique

The difference between how it works now and how it should work, plus what it would take to close that difference. This is usually the thing you actually hand over.

In the proper languageStructured comparison of current and identifying capability, process and system gaps, with the remediation required to close each.

Gateways

The diamonds. A decision point where the flow splits — if this, go here; if that, go there.

In the proper language element controlling divergence and convergence of sequence flow, including exclusive, parallel and inclusive variants.

GDSnot in your notesdefinition

Government Digital Service. The UK government body that sets the rules for how public-sector digital services must be built — the Service Standard and the Service Manual. If you ever work on a government project, this governs everything you do.

In the proper languageGovernment Digital Service. Sets the GOV.UK Service Standard and Service Manual, defining mandatory criteria and assessment gates — alpha, beta, live — for public-sector digital service delivery.

Governancenot in your notesprocess

The structure of who is allowed to decide what, and which forum signs things off. Dull, and the thing that determines whether your requirement gets approved or sits in limbo.

In the proper languageThe framework of decision rights, escalation paths and controls under which work is authorised; is not itself a governance method but enables governance by separating who directs, who manages and who delivers.

Guiding obligationprinciple

A rule you do not opt out of. Every one of them holds on every job, each has already been shown to work, and each gives you something to stand on when you push back.

In the proper language

The principles are guiding obligations. They are universal (they apply to every project), self-validating (they have been proven in practice) and empowering (they give practitioners confidence and the ability to influence).

There are seven, and unless all of them are applied, it is not a PRINCE2 project.

Highlight reportdocument

How the current chunk of work is going, sent up to the people who approved it, on a regular beat.

In the proper languageStage status, from the project manager to the project board. Time-driven — the frequency is set by the board.

How every practice is set outpractice

All seven are laid out to the same pattern, so learning the pattern once tells you what to look for in each.

In the proper language

  • Its purpose
  • Its key relationships with the
  • The that support it
  • Its key concepts and definitions
  • The guidance for managing it effectively
  • Its technique

How the organizing practice applies the principlespractice

Each of the seven rules turns up here as one concrete thing this practice does.

In the proper language

Ensure continued business justification
“Assigning someone from the business to the role who represents the business viewpoint.”
Learn from experience
“Using lessons to inform the project management team structure, , and a healthy ” — so “the right people are in the right roles at the right time”.
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
“Developing an explicit project management team structure that ensures everyone involved is fully aware of their responsibilities and relationships.”
Manage by stages
“Adapting the project management team structure, role descriptions, commercial management approach, communication management approach, and change management approach at stage boundaries.”
Manage by exception
“Empowering those best placed to make decisions to do so at the appropriate point.”
Focus on products
“Ensuring those who will use the are represented on the project management team, and there is an understanding of the required for their successful deployment.”
Tailor to suit the project
“Creating a project management team that is appropriate to the needs of the project and the capability of the organizations and people involved.”

Hybridapproach

Some parts of the same job built one way, other parts the other.

In the proper language“Some elements of the project use a linear-sequential approach, and other elements use an iterative-incremental approach.” For example: linear-sequential for the infrastructure of a service, iterative-incremental for the customer portal users access it through.

Hybrid deliveryprocess

Running part of a project the waterfall way and part of it the agile way. Very common in big organisations, where the money and the deadlines are agreed up front like waterfall but the building happens in sprints.

In the proper languageDelivery approach combining sequential and iterative elements, typically applying stage-gated governance and fixed funding at programme level with agile execution at team level.

Hypercareprocess

The period right after something goes live when the project team stays on hand with extra support, before handing over to the normal helpdesk. Usually a few weeks. It exists because the first fortnight is when everything nobody thought of shows up.

In the proper languageTime-boxed elevated support period immediately following go-live, staffed by the delivery team, with accelerated triage and fix cycles prior to transition into business-as-usual support.

Impact analysistechnique

Working out what else a change will touch before you make it — other systems, other teams, reports, processes nobody mentioned. It's how you avoid breaking three things to fix one.

In the proper languageAssessment of the consequences of a proposed change across systems, processes, data, and groups, used to inform decisions.

Incidentdefinition

Something going wrong with a live service that users are feeling right now.

In the proper languageAn unplanned interruption or reduction in quality of a live service, managed through to restoration under agreed targets.

Incident escalation frameworkprocess

The agreed rules for who gets contacted, how serious it has to be, and how long you wait before waking someone senior up.

In the proper languageDefined escalation paths and thresholds governing handling, tiers, timeframes and authority levels by incident .

Initiating a projectprocess

Where the detail gets worked out, once permission to spend time on it has been given. Most of a business analyst's job lives here — finding out what is needed, working out what should change, and writing it down.

In the proper languageEstablishes solid foundations for the project, enabling the business to understand the work required before committing significant expenditure.

Integrationdefinition

Connecting two systems so that information moves between them automatically instead of somebody re-typing it.

In the proper languageThe connection of discrete systems to exchange data or invoke functions, implemented via , message queues, file transfer or middleware.

Interviewstechnique

Speaking to one person at a time. Good for depth, and for people who will not say what they think in front of their manager.

In the proper languageOne-to-one technique. High depth, low coverage, susceptible to individual bias; usually paired with a broader technique.

ISEBqualification

The old name for the same qualifications. ISEB was absorbed into years ago, so an ISEB certificate and a BCS one are the same family — seeing the old name usually means the person qualified a while back.

In the proper languageInformation Systems Examinations Board. Merged into ; legacy ISEB certifications map to current BCS equivalents.

Two of your CVs list this qualification under different names — that is why.

Issue

Something that has already happened and now needs somebody to decide what to do. Not always a problem — it can be an unexpected chance, or a request to change what was agreed.

In the proper languageAn unplanned event that has occurred and requires management action; the recognised kinds are a problem, an external event, a business opportunity, a request for change and an .

Issue management approachapproach

How things that have already gone wrong get raised, judged and decided — and how changes to what was agreed are controlled.

In the proper language“How issues will be captured and reported, and how changes to the project baseline will be assessed and controlled.” Held in the PID.

Issue registerdocument

The list of what has already happened and is being dealt with formally.

In the proper language“To log issues that are being managed formally, their current status, and date of closure.”

Issue reportdocument

A write-up of one thing that has gone wrong: what it hits, what could be done, and what is recommended.

In the proper languageAn individual issue’s impact on the baseline, the options, and a recommendation.

Iterative-incrementalapproach

The same loop runs over and over, and something usable appears early.

In the proper language“Often, but not exclusively, used for product development where requirements gathering, design, development and/or coding, and testing occur iteratively throughout the lifecycle of the project. This approach is often referred to as an approach.” Here “the project plan may provide multiple delivery stages in which the quality and are refined in parallel with development of the required products through the use of a ”.

ITILqualification

A framework of good practice for running IT services day to day — handling , changes and service levels. Version 5 came out in February 2026.

In the proper languageIT service management framework covering the service value system, practices and continual improvement. Version 5, released February 2026, reframes ITSM as digital and service management.

Gabrielle's CV said v5 and I assumed it was a mistake. It isn't — that CV is recent.

Jirasoftware

The most widely used tool for tracking work in teams. Where the , the and the actually live.

In the proper languageAtlassian work tracking platform supporting management, boards, workflow configuration and defect tracking.

Kanbanprocess

A way of working with no at all — work just flows through columns on a board continuously. Its key rule is limiting how many things can be in progress at once, which stops everything being started and nothing being finished.

In the proper languageFlow-based method using a visual board, explicit work-in-progress limits and continuous delivery rather than fixed iterations. Well suited to support and business-as-usual work with unpredictable arrival rates.

Key influencersrole

The few people you have to work closest with — and who they are changes as the work goes on.

In the proper language

“The people the needs to work closest with to ensure the success of the project.” They “may be the following: senior executives; those found in the user, supplier, or wider operational communities within the organization undertaking day-to-day tasks and decision making”.

And note: “stakeholders at the interface with the project may change over time as the project evolves and relationships develop”.

Leadershipconcept

Getting people to want to do the work.

In the proper language

“Motivating people to achieve a project’s objectives. On projects, this is best done through across the project ecosystem, persuading, influencing, and co-creating with a focus on managing key relationships and seeking regular feedback to ensure team members remain aligned to the project’s objectives and agree to joint ways of working.”

Lean Six Sigmaprocess

Two process-improvement methods used together. Lean is about removing wasted effort; Six Sigma is about reducing variation so results are consistent. Belts — yellow, green, black — indicate how far someone has trained.

In the proper languageCombined methodology pairing Lean waste elimination with Six Sigma variation reduction, executed through the DMAIC cycle. Green Belt denotes practitioner-level competence, typically leading improvement projects part-time under Black Belt supervision.

Learn from experienceprinciple

Look up what happened last time, write down what is happening this time, and hand both on to whoever goes next.

In the proper language

“A PRINCE2 Project Management project team actively seeks, records, and implements improvements as a result of relevant lessons learned from prior projects and throughout the life of the project. It applies them in future projects and shares them for others to apply.”

Three time horizons: lessons from prior projects, lessons during this project, and lessons passed to future projects — and shared with others. A is “information to facilitate the future of the project or other projects and actively promote learning from experience”.

Lessondefinition

Something learned that is worth passing on, either to later parts of this piece of work or to the next one.

In the proper languageInformation to facilitate the future of the project or other projects and actively promote learning from experience.

Lessons logdocument

What is worth knowing next time, gathered from before this job and during it.

In the proper languageLessons identified, from prior projects and from this one. A is “information to facilitate the future of the project or other projects and actively promote learning from experience”.

Lessons reportdocument

What was learned, written up so later work and other jobs can use it rather than repeating it.

In the proper languageLessons for later stages and other projects.

Linear-sequentialapproach

Each step finishes before the next one starts.

In the proper language“Each of the delivery steps to create the products occurs in sequence, and the product is made available during or at the end of the project (for example, in a construction project where requirements gathering and design occur before construction starts).” Here “the should be sufficiently detailed to enable costs and time to be estimated at an appropriate level of confidence”.

Lucidchartsoftware

A diagramming tool that runs in a browser. Same job as , easier to work on with other people at the same time.

In the proper languageWeb-based diagramming platform with real-time collaboration and / stencil support.

Maintain (business case step 3)technique

Put the real numbers in as they arrive, and re-forecast the rest.

In the proper language“The updates the business case with the progress data (such as products delivered, project costs, benefits realized) and the latest forecasted benefits and performance targets.” Done at .

Manage by exceptionprinciple

You are told how far off course you may go, and you go back up only before you exceed it.

In the proper language

“A PRINCE2 Project Management project establishes limits of delegated authority by defining tolerances for performance against its plans.”

It works by “delegating authority from one management level to the next, by setting against the seven aspects of performance (benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, and risk) for the respective level (project, stage, team)”. It “provides for efficient use of senior management time as it reduces senior managers’ time burden without removing their control. This ensures that decisions are made at the right level in the organization.”

The trapYou escalate when a is forecast to be breached — not when something has merely gone wrong.

Manage by stagesprinciple

The work is cut into chunks, and the next chunk needs fresh permission at the end of the one before it.

In the proper language

“A PRINCE2 Project Management project is planned, monitored, and controlled on a stage-by-stage basis.”

A is “the section of a project that the is managing on behalf of the at any one time”. Managing by stages “ensures that the project is properly initiated before work starts on delivery of the project’s outputs”, and it “addresses the need to keep plans within reasonable ”.

Every PRINCE2 project has a minimum of two management stages: an initiation stage, plus at least one delivery stage.

Manage the ongoing changes to the project ecosystem (organizing step 4)technique

People come and go as the work changes shape.

In the proper language“The capabilities required on a project will change over the project lifecycle, requiring the to ensure the supports this, transitioning people onto and off the project as required, and enhancing capacity and capabilities.”

Managementconcept

Telling people what to do and how, in line with what everyone has already agreed.

In the proper language

“Instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working. Co-creating ways of working with project team members (and stakeholders) significantly improves people’s willingness to be managed in line with them.”

The trapLeadership is motivating people towards the objectives; management is instructing the execution of tasks. The adage about leaders doing the right things is not the wording used.

Management approachapproach

A document saying how one part of the work will be run here. If the name ends in “approach”, this is what it is.

In the proper languageA management product describing how something will be managed on this project — its procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities. All nine live in the .

Management productdocument

Anything produced only in order to run the work: a plan, a log, a report. Never the thing the work exists to deliver.

In the proper language

Management products “describe the information that will be required to manage the project”. They are not outputs — they “are created solely for the purpose of managing the project”.

The trapSpecialist products are what the project exists to deliver; management products are how you steer it.

Management products for the business case practicedocument

Four documents: the argument, and how it will be checked.

In the proper language

  • — in the
  • — in the

Management products for the organizing practicedocument

Three documents, and all three sit in the same folder.

In the proper language

All three are held in the .

Managing (management level)concept

The person running it day to day, inside the room they were given.

In the proper languageThe . “Day-to-day control of a stage within the tolerance limits established by the project board.”

Managing a stage boundaryprocess

The point between two chunks of work where you show what got finished, update the numbers, and ask to carry on. It is the honest moment, and the answer is allowed to be no.

In the proper languageGives the what it needs to approve the next and confirm the work is still justified; happens at the end of every except the last.

Managing product deliveryprocess

The step where things actually get built, and it runs at the same time as . Its whole job is the handover in both directions — what a team is asked to produce, and what they hand back as finished.

In the proper languageControls the link between and team manager, agreeing the requirements for acceptance, execution, reporting and delivery of specialist products.

Mermaid / Mermaid AIsoftware

Two related things. Mermaid itself is a way of making diagrams by typing text instead of dragging shapes — you write a few lines describing the steps and it draws the flowchart. Mermaid AI is the paid layer on top: you describe what you want in plain English and it writes those lines for you, then draws it.

In the proper languageMermaid is an open-source text-based diagram definition syntax rendered to SVG, allowing diagrams to be version-controlled alongside source. Mermaid AI is the commercial prompt-to-diagram feature in Mermaid Chart, generating Mermaid syntax from natural-language input.

You wrote “Mermaid Ai?” with a question mark. I first told you it wasn’t an AI tool — that was wrong. The CV was right.

Mironot in your notessoftware

An infinite online whiteboard. Used for — sticky notes, journey maps, rough process flows, especially with people in different places.

In the proper languageCollaborative digital whiteboard supporting real-time multi-user workshops, templated frameworks and freeform diagramming.

MoSCoWtechnique

A way of sorting into four buckets by how essential they are: Must, Should, Could and Won't. The capital letters spell it; the small o's are just to make it pronounceable.

In the proper languagePrioritisation technique originating in DSDM, categorising requirements as Must have, Should have, Could have, or Won't have this time.

Must have

The release genuinely fails without it. If you find that most things are a must, the prioritising has not actually happened.

In the proper languageNon-negotiable without which the release has no viability. Typically capped at around 60% of effort to preserve contingency.

Navisionsoftware

An older Microsoft for mid-sized companies, properly called Dynamics NAV. Now succeeded by Business Central, so seeing it named on a CV suggests older experience.

In the proper languageMicrosoft Dynamics NAV. Mid-market , superseded by Business Central.

Non-functional requirementdefinition

How well the system has to do it, rather than what it does. Speed, security, how often it's allowed to be down, whether a blind person can use it. “It must be fast” is not one of these. “Search returns results in under two seconds with five hundred people using it at once” is.

In the proper languageA requirement specifying a quality attribute or constraint rather than a function — performance, availability, security, scalability, accessibility, maintainability, regulatory compliance. Must be stated with measurable thresholds to be testable.

Observationtechnique

Watching people do the job rather than asking them about it. Catches all the steps people have stopped noticing they do, which is usually where the problems hide.

In the proper language by direct observation of work as performed, sometimes called job shadowing. Effective at surfacing tacit knowledge and workarounds absent from documented process.

Off-specificationdefinition

Something built, or about to be built, that will not meet what was written down for it. Different from a request for a change: nobody asked for this — it just is not going to hit the mark.

In the proper languageA that will not meet its ; like a request for change it is a type of issue, and the decides what to do about it.

OOdefinition

Object-oriented. A way of building software where you model things in the real world as self-contained objects with their own data and behaviour. was designed to draw it.

In the proper languageObject-oriented and design. Paradigm structuring systems as collaborating objects encapsulating state and behaviour, with inheritance and polymorphism.

Operational readinessprocess

Checking that the business is actually ready to use the new thing on day one — people trained, support desk briefed, processes rewritten. Software being finished is not the same as an organisation being ready for it.

In the proper languageAssessment and preparation confirming that people, process and support capability are in place to operate a solution at go-live, covering training, documentation, support model and cutover readiness.

Option assessmentprocess

Laying out the realistic ways of solving the problem and comparing them properly — including doing nothing at all, which is always on the table and occasionally the right answer. Stops the first idea winning by default.

In the proper languageStructured comparison of candidate against defined criteria — cost, , risk, feasibility and time — including the do-nothing , producing a recommendation for approval.

Organizational design and development (the technique)technique

Five steps, running from understanding the ground to handing it all over.

In the proper language

  • Understand the organizational ecosystem
  • Design the project ecosystem
  • Develop the project ecosystem
  • Manage the ongoing changes to the project ecosystem
  • Transition the project into the organizational ecosystem
