Five steps, not four — UDDMT.

DangerA great deal of the material in circulation gives this technique as four steps. There are five.

Organizational ecosystemconcept

Everything that was already there before the work started — how the place is set up and how it does things.

In the proper languageThe wider organization or organizations the project sits inside — their existing structures, , policies, and ways of working.

Organizing (the practice)practice

The part of the work that settles who answers for what, and to whom, before anyone starts.

In the proper language“To define and establish the project’s structure of accountability and responsibilities (the ‘who’).”

The trapThe purpose sentence says the organization practice; the practice itself is called organizing.

Outcomedefinition

What people now do differently because of it. If nobody changed how they work, there is no outcome.

In the proper language“The result of change, normally affecting real-world behaviour and circumstances. Changes are implemented to achieve outcomes, which are achieved as a result of the activities undertaken to facilitate the change.”

Outputdefinition

The thing that got built and handed over. On its own it proves nothing.

In the proper language“The tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity.” What the project builds.

Peopleelement

Everyone doing the work and everyone the work lands on, and how they get on with each other.

In the proper language“Those working on the project and those affected by the project. An understanding of the needs, capabilities and motivations of the people involved and the relationships between them is crucial to how the project is established and managed.”

People affected by the projectconcept

The people who will have to live with the result without having worked on it.

In the proper language

They are “people within the business who are affected by the project, but do not work within the defined project team”. Their characteristic contribution is “integrating new products into their area of the organization”.

So when a question asks who contributes from outside the project team, none of the named PRINCE2 roles is the answer.

People within the projectconcept

Everyone holding a named job on the work, including the ones who only direct it and never touch it.

In the proper language

Everyone in the : , , , , , , , and the team members doing the work.

The trapThe is inside the team — they represent the user community, not the people merely affected. So are the project executive and the team manager.

Personanot in your notesdocument

A short written sketch of a typical user — what they're trying to do, what gets in their way. Used so that discussions are about a specific person rather than a vague “the user”.

In the proper languageResearch-derived archetype representing a user segment, capturing goals, behaviours, context and pain points, used to ground design and prioritisation decisions.

Pivot tabletechnique

An feature that summarises a big list into totals grouped however you like — sales by region, by month, by — without writing any formulas.

In the proper languageExcel feature performing interactive aggregation and cross-tabulation of tabular data across configurable row, column and value dimensions.

Planning horizonconcept

How far ahead you can plan in detail and still be believed. Beyond it you are guessing, so you plan that part roughly and come back to it.

In the proper languageYou can only plan in detail as far ahead as you can reliably foresee — hence a high-level project plan plus a detailed stage plan for the current stage. “The PRINCE2 Project Management principle of manage by stages addresses the need to keep plans within reasonable planning horizons.”

PLMnot in your notessoftware

Lifecycle Management. One system holding everything about a physical product from first sketch to being discontinued — drawings, parts lists, versions, and every change anyone made. Where an runs the business, a PLM runs the product.

In the proper languageProduct Lifecycle Management. System of record for product definition data including files, bills of materials, revision history and engineering change orders, typically with for downstream manufacturing execution.

Portfolioconcept

Everything an organisation is changing at once.

In the proper languageAll the change an organization is running. A project may sit inside a or inside a portfolio; either way that position forms part of its .

Postmannot in your notessoftware

A tool for poking an by hand to see what it returns. Lets an analyst check what data a system actually gives back without needing a developer to run it for them.

In the proper language client for constructing, sending and inspecting HTTP requests, with collection management and automated test scripting.

Power and interestnot in your notestechnique

A way of ranking stakeholders on two questions: how much can they affect this, and how much do they care? The ones high on both get your attention; the ones low on both get an email.

In the proper language grid plotting influence against interest to determine engagement strategy — typically manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, or monitor.

Power BIsoftware

Microsoft's reporting tool. Turns data into dashboards and charts that update themselves.

In the proper languageMicrosoft business intelligence platform for data modelling, DAX-based measures and interactive report distribution.

Practiceselement

The seven things you have to keep doing all the way through.

In the proper languageSeven aspects of project management that “must be applied consistently and throughout the project lifecycle”. Each practice explains the specific treatment that aspect needs for the processes to be effective — and why it is necessary.

PRINCE2definition

A rulebook for running a piece of work: who decides what, at which points, and on what evidence. It does not say how to build anything — only how to stay in control of the building.

In the proper languageA project management method built from five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes and project context.

Principleselement

The seven rules a project has to keep to.

In the proper languageThe seven guiding obligations that determine whether a project is genuinely being managed using PRINCE2. Unless all seven are applied, it is not a PRINCE2 project.

Prioritydefinition

How urgently it needs fixing. A business judgement. These two often disagree: a spelling mistake on the homepage is barely broken at all but might need fixing this afternoon.

In the proper languageClassification of the urgency with which a should be resolved, determined by business impact rather than technical .

Problemdefinition

Something that has already gone wrong and is hurting now.

In the proper languageAn issue with an immediate and negative impact.

Problem definitionprocess

Writing down what is actually wrong before anyone proposes a fix. Sounds obvious, and it is the step skipped most often — people arrive with a already in mind and the problem gets written backwards to justify it.

In the proper languageArticulation of a business problem in terms of observable symptoms, affected parties and measurable impact, stated independently of any proposed solution.

Process mappingtechnique

Drawing out how work actually flows, step by step, so you can see it rather than argue about it. You cannot fix a process you cannot draw.

In the proper languageThe practice of modelling business processes as diagrams showing activities, decision points, roles and handoffs, typically in a standard notation such as .

Process modeldocument

The actual diagram you produce. A picture of how work moves through an organisation.

In the proper languageA formal representation of a business process, expressed in a standard notation and at a defined level of decomposition.

Processeselement

The seven steps the work runs through, start to finish.

In the proper languageSeven processes that “describe the entire project lifecycle, from activities before getting started, through the stages of project delivery, and to the final act of project closure. Each process has checklists of recommended activities and related responsibilities.”

Productdefinition

Anything the project has to produce. Not only the thing being built — the plans, logs and reports count as products too, which is why each one gets a written description of its own.

In the proper languageAny the project must create, split into specialist products, which are what it exists to deliver, and management products, which only control it.

Product backlognot in your notesdocument

The ordered list of everything that hasn't been built yet. Constantly reordered and refined; never finished.

In the proper languageOrdered, continuously refined list of all known work for a , maintained and prioritised by the .

Product breakdown structuretechnique

A map of everything the work has to produce, broken down from the whole into its parts.

In the proper languageA hierarchical decomposition of the products a plan must deliver.

Product descriptiondocument

A written description of one thing being produced: what it is for, what it is made of, and what it has to satisfy before anyone will call it finished. Written before it gets built, not after.

In the proper languageDefines an individual 's purpose, composition, derivation and , and is the basis on which that product is later checked.

Product Ownernot in your notesrole

The person who decides what gets built next and in what order. If you become a in an team, this is the role you work most closely with — and often the one you eventually move into.

In the proper language role accountable for maximising value, owning content and ordering, and acting as the single point of prioritisation authority.

Product registerdocument

The list of everything a plan has to produce, and how far along each one is.

In the proper language“To list all products required of a plan and the status of those products.”

Product-focuseddefinition

The work is organised around the things being produced, and what “good” means for each of them, before anyone decides which activities will produce them.

In the proper languageOne of the four structural features of PRINCE2, following from the focus on products principle: the method defines and delivers products, in particular their user’s quality expectations and requirements.

Programmeconcept

Several pieces of work run together to deliver one bigger change.

In the proper languageA set of related projects delivering a strategic change. Where a project sits inside one, that position forms part of its .

Projectconcept

A group of people put together for a while to produce something, on the strength of an agreed argument for doing it.

In the proper languageA created to deliver one or more business according to an agreed .

Project assurancerole

The check the deciders run for themselves, one strand for each of the three sides.

In the proper language“Project board members are accountable for the assurance of their respective areas of concern (business assurance, user assurance, supplier assurance). The project board is responsible for establishing how project assurance will be undertaken, ensuring clarity in the roles and responsibilities and how those appointed to assurance roles will interact with each other.”

Project boardrole

The group with the authority to say yes — carry on, stop, or allow something outside the limits.

In the proper language“Accountable to the business for the success of the project and has the authority to direct the project within the remit set by the business.” The business, user and supplier interests are brought together on it. It is the ultimate authority for approving changes.

Project briefdocument

The first written statement of the request, put together before anyone commits real money.

In the proper language“To provide a full and firm foundation for the initiation of the project.” Created in ; it contains the outline business case.

Project contextelement

Everything around the project that the method has to be fitted to.

In the proper languageThe environment the project sits in. The principles, practices and processes “are applied by the people involved to ensure that the method is fit for the project context”.

Project controlsdocument

How closely the work is watched: how often it reports, and how far it may drift before someone has to be told.

In the proper language“Reporting frequencies, tolerances, and how PRINCE2 has been tailored for this project.” Held in the PID alongside the tailoring decisions.

Project ecosystemconcept

The group the work itself brings into being, and how those people get on with one another.

In the proper languageThe temporary community the project creates: the people working on it and the relationships between them.

Project executiverole

The one person who carries the can. There is only one, and they come first.

In the proper language“Appointed by the business as the single point of accountability for the project and is ultimately accountable for the success of the project.” Secures the funding. Owns the . There is only one, and they are appointed first.

Project initiation documentationdocument

The folder agreed before the real money is spent. Once agreed it is frozen, and changing it needs permission.

In the proper language

“The project initiation documentation gives the direction and scope of the project and (along with the ) forms the ‘contract’ between the and the .” It “provides the basis for [the project’s] ongoing management”; “it includes the project plan, the business case, and the frequency of highlight reporting”.

Assembled during initiating a project and baselined when the project board approves it. Reviewed and, if necessary, updated at every stage boundary. Changes to it are handled through the .

Project logdocument

The running record of what has actually happened, kept up to date as the work goes on.

In the proper language

“To capture the continually changing records of issues, lessons, products, quality, risk, and other formal/informal actions or events.”

  • Daily log
  • Lessons log
  • Risk register
  • Issue register
  • Quality register
  • Product register

The maintains it as part of controlling a stage.

Project managementconcept

Working out what has to happen, handing it out, watching what comes back, stepping in when it drifts — and keeping people willing to carry on.

In the proper languageThe planning, delegating, monitoring and controlling of all aspects of the project, and the motivation of those involved, to achieve the project objectives within the expected performance targets.

Project management teamrole

Everybody with a named job on the work, from the ones who only decide down to the ones actually building it.

In the proper languageEveryone within the project: project executive, senior user, senior supplier, project manager, team managers, project assurance, project support, and the team members doing the work.

Project management team structuredocument

The picture of who is involved, and how they all fit together.

In the proper language

“To define who is involved in the project, their relationships, and how they will work together.” Held in the .

“Composed of the , , , and and roles.”

The trapIt cannot direct the project; the board does.

Project managerrole

The person running it inside agreed limits, and the one who has to ask when those limits run out.

In the proper language“Has the authority to run the project on behalf of the within the agreed stage tolerances and constraints.” Responsible for , and for making recommendations “having consulted relevant lessons and standards”.

Project mandatedocument

The request that sets everything off. It can be a formal document or an email from someone senior, and it is usually vaguer than you would like.

In the proper languageThe trigger for , provided by the part of the business commissioning the work.

Project plandocument

The plan for the whole job at arm’s length: the big things being produced, roughly when, and roughly what they cost.

In the proper language“A high-level plan showing the major products of the project and when, how, and at what cost they will be delivered.” Created during initiating a project and baselined on approval by the project board, it “provides a baseline against which to monitor progress throughout the life of the project”.

Project productdefinition

Everything the work delivers, taken as one whole rather than as a pile of separate pieces.

In the proper languageThe total output from the project as defined in the project product description.

Project product descriptiondocument

A description of what the project as a whole is meant to produce, and what would make it acceptable. Written roughly during start-up and sharpened while the detail is worked out — not frozen at the first attempt.

In the proper languageDescribes the project's major and what would make them acceptable, holding the , the acceptance criteria and the acceptance methods.

Project supportrole

The people who keep the machinery running so the work can get done.

In the proper language“Responsible for providing services, such as administrative support, facilitating meetings and workshops, advice and guidance on the project tools, planning support, risk management, issue management, and change management.”

Project teamrole

Everyone who has to give the work time, whatever their job title is elsewhere.

In the proper language“All people required to allocate their time to the project.”

The trapThe project team is all people allocating time to it; the management team is board, manager, assurance, support.

Promappsoftware

A tool specifically for storing and maintaining an organisation's , so they stay findable and up to date rather than dying in someone's folder.

In the proper languageNintex Promapp. process management platform providing a central process repository with ownership, versioning and review cycles.

Prototypestechnique

Showing someone a rough version of the thing. People who cannot describe what they want will immediately tell you what is wrong with something in front of them.

In the proper language and technique using low- or high-fidelity mock-ups to make abstract tangible and surface unstated expectations.

Qualityaspect

How good the thing has to be, decided and written down before it gets built rather than argued about afterwards.

In the proper languageAn aspect of project performance. The quality practice exists “to document the user’s requirements of the project products and to establish the means by which they will be met”. A quality tolerance is “the permissible deviation in a product’s quality before escalation is needed”.

Quality assuranceprocess

Somebody from outside checking that the work is being run properly. A check on the way of working, not on the thing produced.

In the proper languageAn independent check that the project is being run properly — a check on the process, usually from outside the project team.

Quality controlprocess

Checking the thing produced against what it was supposed to be, and recording the result.

In the proper languageThe procedures to monitor specific products and their delivery activities to determine whether they comply with relevant standards.

Quality management approachapproach

How the work will decide whether something is good enough, and who does the deciding.

In the proper language“The quality techniques and standards to be applied, and the roles and responsibilities for achieving the required quality specifications and acceptance criteria.” Held in the PID.

Quality registerdocument

The record of every check planned or done, and how each one turned out.

In the proper language“To summarize all quality management activities that are planned or have occurred.” Used by the and as part of reviewing progress.

Quality specificationsdefinition

The measurable version, written for each individual thing being produced: what gets checked, and what it has to hit. This is what somebody inspecting a finished item actually works from.

In the proper languageA description of what gets checked during quality control and the level a finished must meet. Older material calls these quality criteria.

Quality tolerancedefinition

How far short of the agreed standard something can fall before you have to go and tell someone.

In the proper languageThe permissible deviation in a product's quality before escalation is needed.

RACInot in your notestechnique

A grid saying, for each task, who does it, who signs it off, who gets consulted and who just needs telling. Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed.

In the proper languageResponsibility assignment matrix distinguishing Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed parties per activity or deliverable.

RAID logdocument

A single list tracking four kinds of thing that could derail a project: Risks, Assumptions, Issues and Dependencies.

In the proper languageA working convention rather than a defined in any method — PRINCE2 has no RAID log, splitting the same ground across separate registers inside the .

Regression testingtechnique

Re-checking things that already worked, to make sure the new change hasn't broken them. Dull, and the thing that saves you most often.

In the proper languageRe-execution of existing against unchanged functionality following a change, to detect unintended side effects. Commonly automated given repetition.

Regulatory and compliance awarenessnot in your notesprocess

Knowing which laws and industry rules constrain what you're allowed to build. In financial services, healthcare or government this shapes before anyone starts designing.

In the proper languageAwareness of statutory and sector-specific obligations — data protection, financial conduct, accessibility, records retention — that constrain design and generate mandatory non-functional requirements.

Release managementrole

The team that controls what actually goes live, when, and what happens if it goes wrong. Even finished work waits for them.

In the proper languageThe practice of planning, scheduling and controlling the movement of releases into test and live environments, including rollback planning and .

Request for changedocument

A written proposal to change something already agreed. Writing it down is the point: it forces somebody with authority to say yes or no, rather than the change just quietly happening.

In the proper languageA proposal for a change to a , and one of the five recognised types of issue.

Requirementdefinition

A single statement of something the finished thing must do or must be. The basic unit of the whole job.

In the proper languageA documented condition or capability needed by a stakeholder; is narrower still and treats it as a need or expectation that has been written into an approved document.

Requirements decompositionnot in your notestechnique

The actual craft of turning a broad business need into buildable pieces. “Customers should feel informed” becomes a , then several , then a set of technical . Each level gets more precise and each traces back to the one above.

In the proper languageProgressive elaboration of high-level business needs into functional and technical , maintaining bidirectional at each level of decomposition.

This is the process behind Daniel’s margin note — “turning into bus / tech req spec”.

Requirements engineeringprocess

The whole business of working out what needs building — finding it out, writing it down, checking it, and keeping control of it as things change. It's called engineering because you construct requirements out of vague and contradictory statements; they don't exist ready-made.

In the proper languageThe systematic discipline covering , , , and management of across a lifecycle, including and .

Requirements gatheringprocess

A very common phrase for the same activity. Slightly misleading, because gathering suggests the answers are lying about waiting to be picked up. They usually have to be worked out.

In the proper languageColloquial term for . Often deprecated in favour of “”, which better reflects that are constructed rather than collected.

Requirements traceability matrixdocument

A table linking every forward through the whole chain — from the business need that prompted it, to the that describes it, to the test that proves it, to the that accepts it. It exists to prove nothing quietly went missing.

In the proper languageMatrix mapping each requirement bidirectionally to its source business need and to downstream design, build and test , enabling coverage and impact assessment.

Reviewerrole

The person who decides whether something is good enough, against what was written down before it was built.

In the proper languageThe person or group responsible for assessing if a product meets its quality or acceptance criteria.

Risk

Something that might happen and would change things if it did — usually for the worse, though it can equally be an unexpected chance to do better. Either way, it has not happened yet.

In the proper languageAn uncertain event that would affect the achievement of objectives if it occurred, covering threats and opportunities alike, and recorded with a cause, an effect and a named owner.

Risk action ownerrole

The person who actually carries out the agreed response to a risk. Not necessarily the person who owns the risk.

In the proper languageThe nominated owner of agreed actions to respond to a risk. Also called the risk actionee.

Risk appetitedefinition

How much risk an organisation is willing to run in the first place.

In the proper languageThe organization's attitude towards risk-taking.

Risk exposuredefinition

How much of what you are trying to achieve is currently at stake.

In the proper languageThe degree to which a particular objective is at risk.

Risk management approachapproach

How the work will spot and handle things that might happen. The procedure, not the list of them.

In the proper language“How risk will be managed — the specific procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities.” Held in the PID, and distinct from the risk register, which holds the risks themselves.

Risk ownerrole

The person answerable for watching one particular risk and doing something about it.

In the proper languageThe person responsible for the management, monitoring and control of all aspects of a particular risk.

Risk registerdocument

The list of what might happen, good or bad, and what is being done about each one.

In the proper language“A record of identified risks related to the project, including their status and history. It is used to capture and maintain information on all the identified threats and opportunities relating to the project.”

Risk tolerancedefinition

The agreed range within which a risk can move before somebody senior has to be told.

In the proper languageA measurable threshold representing the tolerable range of outcomes for each objective at risk.

Role descriptionsdocument

What each named job answers for, written down.

In the proper languageDescribe “the roles of those in the project management team and their specific responsibilities”. These “should include specific accountability for targets”. Held in the .

Role-baseddefinition

Responsibility attaches to named jobs rather than to whoever happens to be free, so it is always clear who answers for what.

In the proper languageOne of the four structural features of PRINCE2, following from the define roles, responsibilities and relationships principle: the project has defined and agreed roles within a structure engaging the business, user and supplier interests.

Roles personalized, not standardizedrole

A job is shaped around the person holding it, and reshaped when the people around them change.

In the proper language

“Roles and responsibilities should reflect the capability, authority, and availability of the individual undertaking the work and should be considered through the lens of their key relationships. They should be reviewed in the event of any shifts in these key relationships and updated accordingly.”

The consequence: generic, standard are unlikely to be effective.

Root cause analysisnot in your notestechnique

Digging past the obvious symptom to find what actually caused a problem, so you fix the cause rather than the same symptom over and over.

In the proper languageStructured investigation identifying the underlying origin of a fault or failure rather than its presenting symptoms, using techniques such as , fishbone or fault tree analysis.

SAFenot in your notesprocess

A framework for running across many teams at once in a big organisation. Scaled Agile Framework. Turns up constantly on job adverts for large employers.

In the proper languageScaled Framework. Prescriptive model for coordinating multiple agile teams via Agile Release Trains, Program Increment planning and defined portfolio-level roles.

Same capability, different performanceconcept

Two people trained the same will not do the job the same way, and the same person varies with who they work with.

In the proper language“Even when people technically have the same capabilities and competencies, they are likely to perform the same role differently. Sometimes, the same person may perform differently depending on who they are working with.”

SAPsoftware

A very large German software company whose runs the back office of a lot of big organisations. Notoriously complex.

In the proper languageEnterprise software vendor. SAP and S/4HANA are widely deployed in large-enterprise finance, supply chain and manufacturing.

Scopedefinition

What is included in the work, and just as importantly what is explicitly excluded. The excluded list is the half that saves arguments later.

In the proper languageThe sum of the and the activities needed to produce them, as represented by an approved plan — so the effort of managing the work sits inside the scope, not alongside it.

Scope creepdefinition

Extra work quietly getting added without anyone formally agreeing to it. Not usually anyone being difficult — just lots of small “can it also just…” requests that never got written down.

In the proper languageUncontrolled expansion of scope through unmanaged additions; PRINCE2 calls this uncontrolled change and prevents it by updating a plan only once a change has been approved.

Scrumprocess

The most common specific way of doing . Work happens in fixed short blocks with a defined set of meetings and three defined roles.

In the proper language framework structuring delivery into fixed-length with prescribed roles (, , Developers), events and .

Scrum Masterrole

The person responsible for the process running properly and for clearing obstacles out of the team's way. Not a manager of people.

In the proper language role accountable for the framework being understood and enacted, facilitating events, coaching the team and removing impediments.

SDLCprocess

The whole journey a piece of software goes through, from someone first having the idea to the day it gets switched off. Software Development Life Cycle. It's the container; and are two different ways of moving through it.

In the proper languageSoftware Development Life Cycle. The sequence of phases — typically initiation, , design, build, test, deploy, operate, retire — within which a delivery methodology operates.

Senior supplierrole

The person answerable for the thing being sound, and for the people building it.

In the proper language“Accountable for the quality of the products delivered by the suppliers and for the technical integrity of the project.”

Senior userrole

The person answerable for it being what was needed, and for it being taken up afterwards.

In the proper language“Accountable for ensuring that user needs are specified correctly and that the solution meets those needs.” Also responsible for “the successful handover and adoption of products into the business and continued realization of benefits after the project has closed”, and for securing ongoing commitment from the user community.

Seniority across the structureconcept

Someone on the team may outrank the person running the work, which is normal and makes for friction.

In the proper language

“It is not unusual for members of the project team to be more senior than the , potentially causing hierarchical tension.”

And: “some motivational factors may be outside of a project manager’s remit — for example, remuneration and career progression of project team members.”

Service-level agreementdocument

A written promise about how quickly problems will be responded to and fixed once the thing is live, usually with penalties attached if it's missed.

In the proper languageFormal agreement defining measurable service targets — availability, response and resolution times by — together with reporting and remedies for breach.

ServiceNownot in your notessoftware

A large platform for running IT service desks and workflows — where , requests and changes get logged and tracked. The system that practices usually run inside.

In the proper languageEnterprise service management platform providing ITSM workflows for incident, problem, change and request management, plus workflow automation across other functions.

Severitydefinition

How badly the thing is broken. A technical judgement about the damage.

In the proper languageClassification of the technical impact of a on system function, independent of business urgency.

SharePointsoftware

Microsoft's system for storing and sharing documents inside a company. Where the end up.

In the proper languageMicrosoft platform for document management, collaboration and intranet sites, with versioning and permission control.

Should have

Painful to go without, but you would still ship.

In the proper languageImportant but not vital ; omission causes significant inconvenience for which a workaround exists.

Sign-offprocess

The formal moment someone with authority accepts the work. It matters because it is the point where responsibility transfers.

In the proper languageDocumented acceptance that a meets its criteria; in acceptance typically transfers ownership or responsibility from the project or supplier to the , on behalf of the user.

Solid Edge CADsoftware

Siemens engineering design software, used for drawing physical in 3D. Nothing to do with — it tells you which industry that person worked in.

In the proper languageSiemens application for mechanical design. Sector-specific rather than a competency.

Solutiondefinition

Whatever gets built or changed to fix the problem. It does not have to be software — a solution might be a new process, some training, or scrapping a step entirely. Analysts say “solution” rather than “system” deliberately, because assuming the answer is software is the most common early mistake in the job.

In the proper languageThe set of changes to process, people, technology or policy that satisfies a defined business need. Deliberately technology-agnostic terminology, reflecting that should precede solution selection.

Solution architectrole

The person who decides how something will be built technically — which systems, which approach, how the pieces connect. You decide what it must do; they decide how.

In the proper languageRole responsible for the technical design of a within a specific initiative, translating into a technical approach consistent with .

Specialist productdocument

The thing the work actually exists to produce, as opposed to the paperwork that keeps it under control.

In the proper languageA product the project exists to deliver, as distinct from a . Both kinds sit in the once approved.

Specificationdocument

A written description precise enough to build from. The test is simple: could two people read it separately and produce the same thing? If not, it is not a specification yet — it is a wish.

In the proper languageA document defining the required characteristics of a deliverable in unambiguous, verifiable terms. Forms the basis for build and the reference against which acceptance is judged.

Sprintprocess

A fixed block of time, usually two weeks, in which a team commits to finishing an agreed amount of work. Once it starts, nothing new gets added.

In the proper languageTime-boxed iteration of fixed duration producing a potentially releasable increment. Sprint is protected from change once committed.

SQLdefinition

The language used to ask questions of a database. Structured Query Language. A doesn't usually need to write much, but being able to check a number yourself rather than waiting three days for someone else to check it is a genuine advantage.

In the proper languageStructured Query Language. Declarative language for querying and manipulating relational . For analysts, principally used for data profiling, and reconciliation.

Stagedefinition

A chunk of work somebody senior has approved you to get on with. At the end of each one you go back for permission to start the next, which is also the moment the whole thing can be stopped.

In the proper languageThe section of a project the is managing on behalf of the at any one time; there are always at least two.

Stage plandocument

The detailed plan for the chunk of work about to start — what gets produced, by when, by whom, and for how much. Written at the end of the previous chunk, not all of them at the beginning.

In the proper languageA detailed plan used as the basis for project management control throughout a , approved by the before that stage begins.

Stageddefinition

The work is broken into chunks, and permission to start the next one is given only at the end of the last.

In the proper languageOne of the four structural features of PRINCE2, following from the manage by stages principle: the project is planned, monitored and controlled on a stage-by-stage basis.

Stakeholderconcept

Anyone the work touches, anyone who can touch the work, and anyone who merely believes they are affected.

In the proper language

A stakeholder is “any individual, group, or organization that can affect or be affected by (or perceives itself to be affected by) the project”.

They sit inside or outside the business — “trade unions, customers, suppliers, communities, interest groups, banks, or the media”.

The trapNotes routinely drop “or perceives itself to be affected by”. Without that clause the definition is wrong.

Stakeholder engagementtechnique

Work out who cares, how much they count, what to tell them, tell them — then check whether any of it landed.

In the proper language

  • Identifying stakeholders
  • Analysing their interests and influence
  • Planning how to communicate with them
  • Engaging
  • Measuring whether the engagement is working

STARtechnique

Situation, Task, Action, Result. A structure for answering interview questions about your experience. It is not a technique, despite appearing on a CV as though it were.

In the proper languageBehavioural response framework. Not an method; its appearance as an “analysis framework” is a misattribution.

From Gabrielle's CV. Listed there as an analysis framework, which it isn't.

Starting up a projectprocess

The first step, and it happens before the project properly exists. Somebody has asked for something, and the job here is deciding whether there is a worthwhile piece of work in it at all.

In the proper languageConfirms a viable and worthwhile project exists before initiation begins, producing the .

Supplier interestconcept

The side doing the building, whether they are in-house or hired in.

In the proper languageThose providing the skills and resources to build the products. They “may come from within the organization, or external suppliers may be used for their skills and knowledge”. Represented by the .

Surveystechnique

Sending questions out to a lot of people at once. Wide but shallow: good for counting how common something is, bad for understanding why.

In the proper languageQuantitative technique offering broad coverage at low depth. Useful for hypotheses across a large population rather than generating them.

Sustainabilityaspect

Whether what you build stands up environmentally and socially. Judged and limited exactly like cost or time.

In the proper languageThe seventh aspect of project performance and a full area, documented in the , referencing the organization’s environmental, social and governance () goals.

Sustainability management approachapproach

How the work will keep track of its effect on the planet and on people, and report on it.

In the proper languageHow the project’s environmental, social and economic objectives will be managed, measured and reported. Held in the .

Swimlanesnot in your notesdefinition

Horizontal bands across a process diagram, one per person or team. They show who does what — and every point where work crosses from one band to another is a handover, which is where things usually go wrong.

In the proper language construct partitioning a process by participant or role. Cross-lane transitions represent handoffs and are common sites of delay and error.

Tableausoftware

A rival to doing much the same job — turning data into charts and dashboards.

In the proper languageData visualisation and business intelligence platform, strong on exploratory visual of large datasets.

Tailor to suit the projectprinciple

The method gets sized to the job in hand, so a small job gets a lighter version of it.

In the proper language

“PRINCE2 Project Management is applied and tailored to suit the project environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and level of risk.”

The purpose of doing so: “to ensure that project controls are appropriate to the project’s scale, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and risk”.

The trapManage by exception sets tolerances and limits of authority; tailor makes the method itself proportionate. If the sentence mentions a threshold, a limit or escalation, it is manage by exception.

Tailoringconcept

Fitting the method to the job instead of bending the job to fit the method.

In the proper language

“To enable PRINCE2 Project Management to be used for such a wide range of projects, the method is flexible in how it can be used for any given project. Rather than prescribing what to do to align the method to the specific project, PRINCE2 Project Management offers guidance through principles.”

Tailoring “supports the ability to adapt the PRINCE2 Project Management method to the people and organizations involved, rather than attempting to adapt them to the method”. The principles themselves are “likely to be applied in different ways across projects within an organization”.

Tailoring the management productsdocument

The paperwork can be merged together, or written in a different shape.

In the proper language can be combined with one another, and their format changed.

Tailoring the processesconcept

The steps can be made shorter, or fuller.

In the proper languageProcesses can be tailored by simplifying them or by elaborating them.

Tailoring the project controlsconcept

How closely the work is watched, and how often it has to report back.

In the proper languageThe project controls themselves can be tailored, “to ensure that project controls are appropriate to the project’s scale, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and risk”.

Tailoring the rolesrole

One person can hold more than one job, up to a point.

In the proper languageRoles can be combined, within limits — creating “a project management team that is appropriate to the needs of the project and the capability of the organizations and people involved”.

Tailoring the terminologyconcept

The words can be swapped for the ones people here already use.

In the proper languageTerminology can be tailored — the method’s words replaced by “what is common in the company or in the industry in which the project is taking place”.

Tasks

The boxes on the diagram. One thing that someone does.

In the proper languageAtomic activity within a representing work performed by a participant.

Team managerrole

Whoever runs one patch of the building work. The job can be left unfilled.

In the proper languageDelivers “the products to the agreed specifications”. “Coordinates an area of work that will deliver one or more of the that form the .” May be internal or external.

The trapOptional — the project manager can do it.

Temporarycharacteristic

It has a start and a finish, and then it stops existing.

In the proper language“Projects are temporary in nature. When the desired change has been implemented, resumes (in its new form), and the need for the project is removed.” Because they are temporary “they should therefore have a defined start and a defined end”.

Temporary organizationconcept

A group of people brought together to get one thing done, and taken apart again once it is. Not a department and not a permanent team.

In the proper languageThe phrase the definition of a project turns on. A project is a temporary organization created to deliver one or more business products according to an agreed business case — a structure of people, not merely a piece of work.

Test casedocument

One specific thing to try, with what you expect to happen written down beforehand.

In the proper languageA defined set of preconditions, inputs, execution steps and expected results used to verify a specific or behaviour.

The business case lifecycleconcept

Written before the work, checked all the way through, and looked at again once it is over.

In the proper language

The is used to develop the outline business case, which sits inside the .
The outline is developed into the full business case and baselined as part of the .
During each stage
The keeps it under review — “the business case is kept under review” is an explicit objective of — and checks it when assessing progress, risks and issues.
At each
Updated with actual costs, products delivered, benefits realized and the latest forecasts, so the can confirm continued justification before approving the next stage.
Checked to “assess the project’s performance against requirements and the probability that the outcomes will provide the expected benefits”. Any remaining benefit reviews are handed to the business in the .
After closure
Reviewed by the business in a post-project , to confirm whether the intended benefits were realized in practice.

The business case practice and the principlespractice

This is where one of the seven rules actually gets done: write the argument down, then keep checking it.

In the proper languageThe direct expression of the principle. Justification “is established at the beginning of the project through the creation of a business case and then kept under regular review and updated in response to the decisions and events that might impact the desirability, viability, or achievability of the project”.

The business, user and supplier interestsconcept

Whoever pays, whoever uses it and whoever builds it. All three have to have someone speaking for them.

In the proper language

“All projects have the following primary : the business, users, and suppliers. All three stakeholder interests need to be represented effectively in the project management team; this is reflected in the design of a .”

Suppliers “may come from within the organization, or external suppliers may be used for their skills and knowledge”.

The eight PRINCE2 rolesrole

Eight named jobs, and one of the eight is optional.

In the proper language

The five characteristics of a projectcharacteristic

The five things that make it a project rather than .

In the proper language

  • Change
  • Cross-functional
  • Unique
  • Uncertainty
  • Temporary

Memory hook

C
Change
C

U

Temporary

That is the order to learn them in, not the order they are usually listed in.

The trapThe precise phrasing is what counts. Unique still allows similar projects to a proven pattern; riskier means riskier than business as usual, not risky outright; and temporary is tied to business as usual resuming, not to any fixed duration.

The five integrated elementselement

The five parts the method is built from. They only work together.

In the proper language

  • Principles
  • People
  • Practices
  • Processes
  • Project context

DangerThere are five. Some practice questions in circulation are out of date and reflect the old syllabus, which had four — if you meet one of those, count and back in.

The five things you can tailorconcept

What you are allowed to change when you fit the method to the job.

In the proper language

  • Processes
  • Management products
  • Roles
  • Terminology
  • Project controls

Two worked examples: “requiring only those quality activities that are appropriate to the delivery method and product characteristics”, and creating “a project management team that is appropriate to the needs of the project and the capability of the organizations and people involved”.

The four management levelsconcept

Four rungs, each with less room than the last.

In the proper language

“The project is between four management levels against tolerances for seven .”

Commissioning
The , outside the project team
Directing
The
Managing
The
Delivering

The principles in the people elementprinciple

Six principles have a people sentence attached, and the wrong answers are the other five sentences.

In the proper language

“There is valuable knowledge hidden within a project ecosystem. This requires a collaborative environment that encourages knowledge sharing throughout the lifetime of a project.” And: “people factors such as behaviours, culture, and relationships are difficult to document and are best learned through social learning.”
“Decisions should be made at the most local level where the knowledge needed to make and own those decisions resides. Decisions should be progressed through the levels when a decision has the potential to impact other areas of the project.” And: “the extent of delegation is often dependent on the level of confidence and trust that exists in the key relationships.”
Ensuring “people factors are continually addressed throughout the project’s lifecycle”.
“The stages of a project often mark a change in the influencers and any key relationships. They are good points to review how the project is planned to deliver.”
“Co-creating products, with agreed product descriptions, with the business, user, and supplier communities unites their different perspectives. This improves the development and adoption of the products into the business, reducing handover risks and ensuring that operational and maintenance issues are fully considered.”
“Tailoring supports the ability to adapt the PRINCE2 Project Management method to the people and organizations involved, rather than attempting to adapt them to the method.”

The principles inside each practiceprinciple

Every practice shows how it applies all seven, one line each.

In the proper language

Each of the seven sets out how it applies every one of the seven principles.

The seven aspects of project performanceaspect

The seven things a project is judged on, and the seven you can set a limit against — at project, stage and team level.

In the proper language

Tolerances are set “against the seven aspects of performance (benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, and risk) for the respective level (project, stage, team)”.

The trapSustainability is the seventh aspect; people is an integrated element, not an aspect at all.

The seven practicespractice

Seven things you have to keep doing all the way through, each answering one question about the work.

In the proper language

Business case Why?
Judge whether the project is, and remains, desirable, viable and achievable.
Organizing Who?
Define and establish accountability and responsibilities.
Plans How, when, how much?
Define the products and the means to deliver them.
Quality What good looks like
Document the user’s requirements and establish how they will be met.
Risk What if?
Identify, assess and control uncertainty.
Issues What now?
Collect and assess issues, and control changes to the baseline.
Progress Where are we?
Monitor against plan, forecast, and control deviations.

Issues

“Because Our Products Quite Rarely Interest People”.

The seven principlesprinciple

Seven rules, and a piece of work has to satisfy every one of them before it counts as one of these.

In the proper language

  • Ensure continued business justification
  • Learn from experience
  • Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
  • Manage by stages
  • Manage by exception
  • Focus on products
  • Tailor to suit the project

Memory hook

C
Continued business justification
D
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
L
Learn from experience
M
Manage by stages
M
Manage by exception
F
Focus on products
T
Tailor to suit the project

“Cats Definitely Like Meals Made From Tuna”. Learn from experience is numbered second and define roles third; the sentence takes them the other way round.

The three families of management productdocument

Every one says one of three things: how it is run, what happened, how it goes.

In the proper language

“How will X be managed on this project?”
Procedures, techniques, standards, responsibilities → a , in the .
“What is the record / status / history of X?”
A register or log, in the .
“Telling someone how it is going”
A report — , , , , , or .

The trapThe quality register holds the checks and their results; the product register holds each product’s status. And the holds the risks, where the holds the procedure for handling them.

The three project interestsconcept

Three sides have to be in the room: whoever pays, whoever uses, whoever builds.

In the proper language

“All projects have the following primary stakeholders: the business, users, and suppliers. All three stakeholder interests need to be represented effectively in the project management team; this is reflected in the design of a .”

Business
Represented by the
User
Represented by the
Supplier
Represented by the

The two ecosystemsconcept

One is the world the work lands in; the other is the world the work brings into being.

In the proper language

  • Organizational ecosystem
  • Project ecosystem

The relationship is stated directly: “projects unite people from organizations that already have defined organizational structures and corporate governance requirements. An understanding of the organizational ecosystem is required to successfully design the project organization and determine how the project ecosystem will develop as a distinct entity from the organizational ecosystem.”

The two people management productsdocument

Two documents: one about getting people to adopt the change, one about who is told what, and how often.

In the proper language

  • Change management approach
  • Communication management approach

Both live in the , and both are reviewed and adapted at stage boundaries, along with the and .

The value chainconcept

What you build only counts once it is used, and something measurable improves because of it.

In the proper language

“PRINCE2 Project Management projects deliver outputs in the form of products which are used to facilitate changes in an organization or for organizations. These changes create capabilities that lead to outcomes. The outcomes allow the organization(s) to realize the benefits that are explained in the business case for the project. Outcomes that are perceived as negative by one or more stakeholders may result in dis-benefits.”

Output → change → capability → outcome → benefit → business objective. A negative outcome gives a dis-benefit.

The trapAn outcome leads to a benefit, and the benefit is what contributes to a business objective — never from an outcome straight to a business objective.

Timeaspect

How long the work is allowed to take. One of the seven things a project is judged on.

In the proper languageAn aspect of project performance. Tolerances are set against it at project, stage and team level, and actual progress is measured against its performance target.

Time-driven controldefinition

A check that happens because a date has come round, rather than because something specific has happened.

In the proper languageA control occurring at regular intervals, such as the checkpoint report and highlight report.

To-bedefinition

How the process should work once you've fixed it. Always drawn after the , never before, or you end up designing around problems that were never there.

In the proper languageTarget-state representing the intended future process following the proposed change.

TOGAFdefinition

The Open Group Architecture Framework. A widely used rulebook for how a large organisation should structure its technology — what connects to what, and how anything new has to fit in. Where a company has standards, they are usually based on this.

In the proper languageThe Open Group Architecture Framework. Enterprise architecture methodology comprising the Architecture Development Method, a content framework and a capability model.

Tolerancedefinition

How far off you are allowed to drift before you have to go and tell someone. Being inside it is what lets you get on with the work without asking permission for every decision.

In the proper languageThe permissible deviation from a plan before escalation to the next is required, set against time, cost, scope, quality, , risk and sustainability.

Trade-offs between performance targetsconcept

Pushing one target up pushes another one out. They are weighed together, not one at a time.

In the proper language

“All seven aspects of the project’s performance targets and their relationships with each other should be considered as part of assessing the business justification, but there will often be trade-offs between different performance aspects. For example, if in developing the project product description it is decided that higher quality targets are required, it is likely to impact the cost, time, or sustainability targets.”

The seven are the .

Transition the project into the organizational ecosystem (organizing step 5)technique

Hand the whole thing back to the business at the end.

In the proper languageAt close, understand the ecosystem the products and remaining team members will transition into. “There are three key aspects the needs to consider as part of the transition: products, people, and learning.”

Triageprocess

Sorting problems into what gets dealt with first. Borrowed from hospitals. It is about deciding the order, not about diagnosing the cause.

In the proper languageThe process of assessing and prioritising or for resolution, assigning , and ownership.

Ray's CV glossed this as “prioritising issue resolvement”, which is right.

UATprocess

The where actual users try the thing and say whether it does what they asked for. User Acceptance Testing. Note this is a different question from whether it works — software can pass every technical test and still be the wrong software.

In the proper languageUser Acceptance Testing. Final phase in which business representatives execute scenarios derived from to confirm the meets the specified need, culminating in formal .

UAT planningprocess

Deciding up front who will test, which situations they'll try, what counts as a pass, and who is allowed to say yes at the end.

In the proper languagePreparation of the approach — , entry and exit criteria, scenario set, participants, environment, data, process and authority.

UMLdefinition

A different diagram language, for describing software rather than business processes. Unified Modeling Language. Where asks who does what, UML asks how the system is put together.

In the proper languageOMG standard notation for modelling software systems, comprising structural diagrams (class, component) and behavioural diagrams (sequence, state, activity).

Uncertaintycharacteristic

More can go right or wrong than in the day job.

In the proper language“The characteristics already listed will introduce threats and opportunities over and above those typically encountered within . Projects are riskier than any operational aspects of an organization.”

Understand the organizational ecosystem (organizing step 1)technique

Find out what structures already exist before designing anything new.

In the proper language“Projects unite people from organizations that already have defined organizational structures and corporate governance requirements. An understanding of the is required to successfully design the project organization.” Clarify who retains responsibility for policies, procedures and ways of working.

Uniquecharacteristic

No two are the same, even when they look the same.

In the proper language“Every project is unique. An organization may undertake many similar projects and establish a familiar, proven pattern of project activity, but each one will differ in a certain way” — a different team, customer, supplier, product, location or timeframe.

Use casedocument

A written walkthrough of one complete interaction between a person and a system, including what happens when it goes wrong. Useful when the order of steps matters more than the rule.

In the proper languageStructured of an interaction between an actor and a system to achieve a goal, comprising actor, preconditions, main flow, alternate flows and postconditions.

User interestconcept

The side that will actually use the thing, or get the good out of it.

In the proper languageThose who will use the products, operate them, or realize the benefits from them. Represented by the .

User storydocument

A very short description of something a user needs, written in a fixed shape: as a [type of person], I want [something], so that [reason]. The last bit is the one people skip and the one that matters, because it tells you why.

In the proper languageLightweight format used in delivery, expressing need from a user perspective. Sized to be deliverable within one and accompanied by .

User's quality expectationsdefinition

What the people who asked for it say “good” would look like, in their own words. Usually vague and unmeasurable, which is fine — it is the raw material the measurable version gets built from.

In the proper languageA statement of the quality expected from the project , captured in the .

Validationdefinition

Checking you built the right thing. Not the same as verification, which asks whether you built it correctly against the spec. Something can be flawlessly built and still be the wrong thing entirely — validation is the question that catches that.

In the proper languageConfirmation that a deliverable satisfies the actual business need and intended use. Distinct from verification, which confirms conformance to the written .

Visiosoftware

Microsoft's diagramming program. Widely used for because most large organisations already have it.

In the proper languageMicrosoft diagramming application supporting , and flowchart stencils. Desktop-based with limited real-time collaboration.

Waterfallprocess

Doing the strictly one after another: work everything out, write it all down, build it all, test it all, release it. Changing your mind late is expensive, because everything downstream was built on the earlier decisions.

In the proper languageSequential delivery with defined phase gates and a fully specified established before build; PRINCE2 is not a synonym for waterfall, being a management method that sits above any delivery shape.

What an effective team requiresconcept

A mix of people whose skills actually match what this job needs.

In the proper language

Building “an effective team will require a diverse set of capabilities, competencies, and perspectives that match the requirements of the project”.

  • Same capability does not mean same performance
  • Roles should be personalized, not standardized
  • Gaps are closed by upskilling, not by swapping people out
  • Seniority can cut across the structure

What cannot be tailoredconcept

No rule can be dropped and no practice skipped. What changes is how much of each one you do.

In the proper language

All seven principles must be applied or it is not a PRINCE2 project. The likewise “must be applied consistently and throughout the project lifecycle” — what you adjust is the treatment they receive, not whether they happen at all.

DangerAn answer option reading “practices that are not relevant to the project can be excluded” is wrong. It is wording from an older syllabus and it does not hold here.

What is inside the PIDdocument

Nine documents saying how each part of the work will be run, plus the argument, the plan and the people.

In the proper language

The nine management approaches. · · · · · · · · .

Plus. The · the · the · the · the (including reporting frequencies) · the · the .

Where a BA sitsrole

PRINCE2 has no business analyst. You sit inside the project team, and the person your work has to satisfy is the — the one answerable for what is needed being written down correctly.

In the proper languageBusiness analysis is not a named role; analysts work within the project team, support the senior user, and may hold a user assurance responsibility.

Where communication actually happensconcept

Most of it happens off the official channels, so you feed those instead of fighting them.

In the proper language

“Most communication within organizations occurs outside of formal channels. Therefore, it is best to accept this and provide information in multiple formats that people can share easily and provide multiple pathways for people to give feedback.”

“The communication management approach is likely to evolve as the project evolves and becomes more defined.”

Where tailoring decisions are documenteddocument

In the folder agreed before the real money is spent — the .

In the proper language

“How PRINCE2 Project Management will be applied and tailored for the particular project is captured in the .”

The trapThe , the and the are all three offered as wrong answers.

Who is responsible for tailoringrole

The person running the work proposes it; the people who authorise the work agree it.

In the proper language

“The is responsible for tailoring and will make recommendations having consulted relevant lessons and standards.”

The project manager proposes; the , as the body accountable for the project, agrees the approach as part of approving the .

Why project management is usedconcept

Change pushed through the normal chain of command fails in the same handful of ways every time.

In the proper language

Change delivered through normal line management tends to fail in predictable ways: unclear objectives and scope, no agreed justification, poor estimation, undefined roles, uncontrolled change, unmanaged risk, and stakeholders who were never engaged.

PRINCE2 addresses exactly those failure modes: a documented justification, defined roles across business, user and supplier, product definitions agreed before work starts, controlled with , and an explicit route for escalating problems.

WIP limitnot in your notesdefinition

A cap on how many jobs can be underway at the same time. Counter-intuitive but it makes things finish faster, because starting a fifth job doesn't make the first four go quicker.

In the proper languageWork-in-progress constraint applied per board column, used to expose bottlenecks and reduce cycle time by limiting concurrent work.

Wireframenot in your notesdocument

A deliberately rough sketch of a screen layout, showing where things go without any styling. Rough on purpose, so people comment on the structure rather than the colours.

In the proper languageLow-fidelity representation of interface layout and content hierarchy, excluding visual design to focus feedback on structure and flow.

Won't have

Agreed to be out of this time round. It does not mean never — and writing it down explicitly is what stops it quietly reappearing in three weeks.

In the proper language formally excluded from the current delivery but retained on record for potential future consideration.

Work breakdown structuretechnique

A map of the work, hanging off the products.

In the proper language“A hierarchy of all work to be done during a project that forms a link between the and the … supporting the project manager in determining how to structure project teams and the boundaries between them.”

The trapAn organizing concept, not a plans one, and its purpose is about structuring teams.

Work packagedocument

The parcel of work handed to a team, saying what to produce, to what standard, by when, and what to report back. It is the boundary between the person planning and the people building.

In the proper languageA description of the work handed to a team manager, defining the required, their , constraints, reporting arrangements and .

Workshop facilitationnot in your notestechnique

Running a meeting so it actually produces something. A named skill in its own right — keeping the loudest person from dominating, making sure the quiet expert gets heard, and ending with decisions rather than a nice chat.

In the proper languageThe practice of designing and running structured group sessions to reach defined , managing participation, conflict and decision-making without contributing content oneself.

Workshopstechnique

Getting a group in a room together. The real value is that disagreements surface early, while they are still cheap to resolve.

In the proper languageFacilitated group session. Efficient for reaching consensus and exposing conflicting , but requires active facilitation to avoid dominance by senior voices.
